html:
The Mikve Israel-Emanuel synagogue in Willemstad, Curacao, built in 1732, is the oldest synagogue in continuous use in the Americas. Its floor is covered with sand.

Its congregation was founded in 1651 by Sephardic Jews, descendants of Jews expelled from Spain and Portugal, many of whom had lived in Amsterdam or Dutch Brazil. In the 1700s Curacao had the largest Jewish community in the Americas.

The merchants of the congregation traded across the Caribbean, and its members helped found Jewish communities in New York and elsewhere. The sand is said to recall the Israelites' years in the desert, or the secret worship of Jews under the Inquisition in Spain and Portugal, part of the long story of Judaism in the diaspora.
sum: The Mikve Israel-Emanuel synagogue in Willemstad, Curacao, built in 1732, is the oldest synagogue in continuous use in the Americas. Its floor is covered with sand.
